short: A readable stand-in that copies what one part of a model does, so researchers can follow the computation.
definition: A transcoder is a small, deliberately readable network trained to reproduce what a chunk of a larger model does — take the same input, give roughly the same output — but using a long list of features that each stand for a recognizable concept. Where a sparse autoencoder describes what a model is representing at one point, a transcoder describes a step the model takes, which is what lets researchers follow a computation from one stage to the next. Cross-layer transcoders, which span several layers at once, are the machinery behind circuit tracing and attribution graphs. The trade-off is that the stand-in is never a perfect copy, so conclusions drawn from it have to be checked against the real model.
